topic.angle: From source code to machine instructions

panels.text: People write code in high-level languages, such as FORTRAN or COBOL.
A compiler translates the source code from a high-level language into a low-level one, such as assembly, object code or machine code.
The output is an executable program.
In May 1952, Grace Hopper's team at Remington Rand wrote the compiler for the A-0 language and coined the term. It worked more like a loader or linker than a modern compiler.
